chapter: Louisville, Buck and the carnival years
title: Studying the Bible: where right and wrong began
summary: He says he is religious, not fanatical, and gives his reading of the Devil, God and the origin of right and wrong.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I think so. Not a fanatic, though. Not a fanatic about it, no. I read the Bible a while, pretty good, because I -- do you know about the Bible? Do you know where right and wrong began? No? I wonder why. I wonder why, George. You don't take time out to think about where right and wrong began. So many people want to do right and so many people want to do wrong. You should try to find out where it began. I did. It's my business to find out where it began.
When did you find that out?
When did you find that out?
Oh, a long time ago. Long time ago.
What was it about that question that made you want to investigate? The answer to it.

Because there was so much that was wrong that they try to make right and there's so much that's right that they try to make wrong. That's why. You find so many people think they're right when they're wrong. So many peoples' wrong think they're right. You find that, don't ya? Okay. I want to find out where it began. But the Devil wanted everything to go his way, but God wanted to go the way he wanted to go, where he wanted it.
